author: scolton
body:
I'm pretty sure that this might ruffle some feathers, but it's something I find important.
People these days (and since forever really) haven't always fit into this human invented construct of "gender."  Now we have people being open about not fitting into the the gender binary of "male" and "female" or people whose gender identities can change.  There are two ways to fix the "gender" dropdown on Avicus to make it more politically correct:
  1. Change it to "sex."  Sex is biological, while gender is human invented.  Your gender doesn't necessarily have to align with your sex. Those whose gender identities align with their sex are called "cisgender," while anything else falls under an umbrella called "transgender." However, simply changing to "sex" would still require an addition of an option: intersex. It's especially important at the ages at which Minecraft is played to see an intersex option because it's more common than most realize, and it's generally left alone until post puberty. 
  2. Add more options.  I'd like to see "genderfluid", "genderqueer", and "neither".
I know a lot of people will disregard this as a nonissue but I think it's very important to stay with the times, and other websites (Facebook included) have begun a change to their "gender" policies to help conform to more users.

Also I'd like an email box under contact options.  I mean, I know it isn't the most glamorous way to communicate in this day and age, but it's still a very important and professional form of communication.

replies.author: scolton
replies.body: You're being incredibly insensitive.  It's not about whether people care about you, it's about you having the ability to express yourself.  Non-cisgendered people already face enough discrimination on a daily basis, and it's just that much harder to go on Minecraft, where I generally find that people are very accepting, and not be able to find an option for your gender identity.  I'm not asking for a "sexual orientation" box; I don't think that's helpful here.  And again I'll try to explain this to you: gender has nothing to do with your outward appearance.  At all, ever.  Having a "d***" has nothing to do with your gender.
